meta.auditor: Senior Application Security Engineer (deep-dive; SAST + manual taint analysis)
meta.summary_paragraph: Overall posture is mixed: strong webhook signature handling, but a critical unauthenticated signing endpoint and weak secret management raise the risk profile.

area_assessments.summary: A live secret is committed and shipped to the browser.
An unauthenticated endpoint signs discount tokens the checkout trusts.
SQLi sinks exist in code but are runtime-mitigated.
Payment webhook signatures verified before processing.
Debug dashboard exposed on a non-production host.

verification_changes.reason: Model applies a global tenant_id scope, so not cross-tenant exploitable.

meta.sast_summary: npm audit -> 12 advisories (2 high); semgrep -> 9 results; gitleaks -> committed dev env file.

remediation_steps.title: Authenticate the signing endpoint
instructions: Add authentication middleware to the sign route.
Validate every discount against a persisted, approved offer.

findings.title: Broken Authentication -> Signed-Coupon Forgery
findings.short_description: An unauthenticated endpoint signs an attacker-supplied discount token with the real COUPON_SIGNING_SECRET.
description_repro: The checkout accepts a discount only if it is a JWT signed with the coupon secret.
The sign route has no authentication middleware.
An attacker submits an arbitrary discount and receives a validly signed token -> free goods.
findings.suggested_fix: Authenticate the caller; validate every discount against a persisted, approved offer; rotate the secret.

findings.title: SQL Injection (authenticated) - code-confirmed, NOT reproducible at runtime
findings.short_description: Three search endpoints interpolate a user-supplied term into a raw LIKE clause.

locations.snippet: db.query(`SELECT * FROM tags WHERE LOWER(value) LIKE '%${term}%'`)

findings.description_repro: Sources are validated only as a 2-255 character string with no character filtering; in source, a crafted term would escape the LIKE string.
findings.verification_note: Runtime: no payload executed; a lone quote returned 200 not a 500, so the quote does not reach the database unescaped in the deployed path. A WAF in front of the app is the likely neutralizer. Fix as defense-in-depth.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind parameters and escape LIKE metacharacters on all three sinks; audit every raw query.
